chunks: And with this chain, from Mustafad ibn Yahya who said: Zakariyya narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Aban al-Qammat, who said: Muhammad ibn Ziyad narrated to us, from Uqbah, from al-Amir al-Juhani, who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) entered the mosque while we were sitting, including Abu Bakr, Umar, and Uthman, and Ali (peace be upon him) was in a corner. The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) came and sat next to Ali (peace be upon him), and began looking to the right and left. Then he said: 'Indeed, on the right of the Throne and on the left of the Throne, there are men upon platforms of light, their faces shining with light.' He said: Abu Bakr stood up and said: 'I sacrifice my father and mother for you, O Messenger of Allah, am I one of them?' He said to him: 'Sit down.' Then Umar stood up to him and said to him the same thing, and he said to him: 'Sit down.' When Ibn Mas'ud saw what the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said to them, he stood up until he stood firm on his feet, then said: 'I sacrifice my father and mother for you, O Messenger of Allah, describe them to us so that we may recognize them by their description.' He said: He struck the shoulder of Ali (peace be upon him) and said: 'This man and his Shia, they are the winners.'
ai.seo_question: Who did the Prophet identify as the winners standing near the Throne?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Fadail al-Shia* highlights the early recognition of Ali ibn Abi Talib’s unique status through the Prophet’s deliberate seating beside him and his subsequent identification of Ali and his *Shi'a* as the 'victorious' (*al-fa'izun*) near the Divine Throne. The narrative underscores the Shia scholarly view that the 'Shi'a of Ali' are not merely political followers but a divinely designated group destined for salvation, distinct from the broader companions like Abu Bakr and Umar who were present but not included in this specific honor.

en.badr-shahin: (The same previous series of relaters) … from Mustafad bin Yahya from Zakariyya from Yahya bin Eban al-Qammat from Mohammed bin Ziyad that Aamir al-Juhani related:

The Prophet (s) entered the mosque while we, including Abu Bakr, Omar, Othman, and Ali, were sitting there. He sat next to Ali (a) and looked to the right and left. He (s) then spoke: There will be some men standing to the right and left of the Divine Throne on luminous stages. Their faces will be glittering. Abu Bakr stood up and said: I sacrifice my father and mother for you, Allah’s Messenger. Will I be one of them? He (s) said: Sit down. Omar, then, repeated the same question of Abu Bakr, and the Prophet (s) to these two men, Ibn Mas’oud stood up and said: O Allah’s Messenger, describe them for us so that we will recognize them. The Prophet (s) stroke the shoulder of Ali and said: They will be this man and his Shia. They will be the winners.
